study: SlideSpeech selective re-decoding, paired lexical marker audit
analysis_type: Retrospective analysis of the frozen SlideSpeech sample. Marker rules fixed before inspecting per-window marker results.
question: How many number and negation marker repairs and new marker errors accompany the net WER gains?
cohort: Keep all 24 frozen windows, nine selected windows, six source videos, and 1,212 words in the original WER comparison. Join first-pass strings in short-call frame order. Compare first with full on all windows; compare first with energy on the same denominator, using full only on originally selected windows.

extraction.normalization: Apply NFKC, casefold, and map curly apostrophes to ASCII. Extract lexical markers only in their original order within each window.
extraction.number_equivalence: Strip thousands commas, insignificant leading zeros and trailing fractional zeros. Cardinal and ordinal remain distinct. Convert listed words to numeric values. Combine a cardinal tens word with an adjacent one-to-nine cardinal or ordinal word across whitespace or hyphens. The component scales are counted individually and longer spoken numerals are not parsed.
extraction.negation_equivalence: The listed words keep their own marker identities. The listed alias and words ending in the frozen suffix map to not. Context, scope, double negation and meaning are outside the extraction.

alignment: Compute unit-cost per-type Levenshtein separately for first and full against the same reference marker sequence for each window. Backtrack with diagonal exact or substitution, then reference deletion, then hypothesis insertion, in that precedence order among optimal predecessors. Indices are one-based, local to type and window.
gross_accounting: A reference slot transitioning from substitution/deletion to exact is a repair, and an exact slot becoming substitution/deletion is a regression. Cancel identical inserted markers as a multiset within the window. Count remaining lost insertions as repairs and remaining gained insertions as regressions. A marker still wrong at the same reference slot is uncorrected. Net repairs must equal first minus candidate edit distance.
reports: Report reference-marker counts, insertion/deletion/substitution counts, gross repairs and regressions, net gain and window counts for each type and condition. Preserve all paired change events as numeric marker positions and operation types, without marker strings. The first repair and regression by frozen manifest order for each type and condition are the display examples, if present. Report zero support explicitly.
failures: Require the same original input and reference hashes and complete matching call schedule. Preserve the earlier input-preparation failure and original call statuses. Reject missing, duplicate and failed calls instead of treating evidence loss as a marker event.
limits: Markers are a narrow text proxy. Ambiguous words such as one and second, grouped or unusually formatted numbers, omitted units and signs, and negation scope can change interpretation. Subsequence alignment cannot establish which concept a marker modifies or judge term correctness. Ties and moved insertions can change event attribution. This is a retrospective six-video audit of one set of cached outputs, with no additional ASR, audio adjudication, classroom validation or product switch.
